note: A demo week for an advanced guitarist: four practice days of about 30 minutes. A mode is drilled by the one note that sets it apart, and that method is the key skill on all four days in new forms: Dorian's 6th found and aimed for over D7, triad notes as targets in a Dorian solo, a Dorian tune made up on the improvisation tool, then Mixolydian's ♭7 and the modes from one root (the mix exercise). Triads on four string sets, the five CAGED shapes of one chord, 9th chords and comping over the backing track feed the solos, and each day opens with a short technique warm-up.

plan.title: Week 1: one note makes the mode
plan.summary: Four practice days of about 30 minutes. Day 1 finds the 6th that makes A Dorian and aims for it over Am7 and D7. Day 2 plays Am and D as triads on four sets of strings and lands a solo on their notes. Day 3 joins the five shapes of one chord and makes up a Dorian tune. Day 4 finds the ♭7 that makes A Mixolydian, then plays the modes from one root.
plan.progress:
Techniques: string skipping and down-up picking in stages, hammer-ons and pull-offs with fingers 3 and 4, the finger order 1, 4, 2, 3. Next: string skipping with three notes a string.
Extended chords: Am7 and D9; Am9, D9 and Gmaj7; the Dorian vamp comped over the backing track. Next: Dm9 and G9.
Scales: A Dorian by its 6th, aimed for over Am7 and D7; triad notes as landing places in a Dorian solo; a Dorian tune of their own; A Mixolydian by its ♭7; the modes from one root; notes named over the whole neck. Next: the Dorian positions joined, then Dorian in D.
CAGED: Am and D triads on four sets of strings; one chord in five shapes up the neck. Next: A, G and D triads.
